newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to auction zero coupon bonds May 7.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to auction zero coupon bonds May 7.

text.p: Thailand's central bank said on Friday it would on May 7 auction one billion baht in seven-year zero coupon bonds to raise funds to help out the cash-strapped property and financial sectors.
"Bidding in the auction will be on May 7 and settlement date will be May 8. The bonds will mature on May 10, 2004," a senior Bank of Thailand official told Reuters.
Next week's auction will feature the first tranche of bonds to be sold from a total issue of 50 billion baht in zero coupon bonds approved by the Thai cabinet this week.
Those eligible to bid in the auction would be the same parties currently approved to bid for central bank short term notes, the official said.
He added that the bonds would be freely transferrable in the secondary market.
"This is the inaugural issue and we will hold more of them in the future. There will be flexibility," he said.
Proceeds from the bonds with seven-year maturity would be used to purchase non-performing property loans from banks and finance companies, aiding cash-strapped property firms.
The bond issue is to be managed by the government-run Property Loans Management Organisation (PLMO).
